title: Practice Lab
blurb: Variables, functions and the event loop.
icon: data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'><rect width='64' height='64' rx='14' fill='%231b5fa8'/><text x='32' y='43' font-family='Menlo,Consolas,monospace' font-size='30' font-weight='700' fill='white' text-anchor='middle'>>_</text></svg>
outcomes: Store values in well-named variables and trace how they change
Define functions with parameters and use the values they return
Build a while True event loop that reacts to button presses
Read a flowchart and turn a plan into pseudocode and Python

topics.title: Variables
topics.lead: A variable is a name that refers to a value. Think of a labelled box: you put a value in with = and use the label later.

acts.title: Predict, then trace
acts.brief: Read the program and decide what the micro:bit will scroll. Lock in your answer, then step through one line at a time and watch the variable boxes change.

acts.title: Arrow animation
acts.brief: This is the class activity from the slides. Build the sequence with the arrow buttons and the code writes itself.

acts.title: Name it well
acts.brief: Descriptive names make code easier to read and fix. Pick the best name for each value. The last question checks Python's naming rules.

acts.title: Quick quiz: what's in the box?
acts.brief: Read each short program and choose what it does. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Dry run the plan
acts.brief: Predict what the plan displays, then watch a dry run fill in the trace table, one line at a time.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program has one bug. Read what it should do and what actually happens, click the line with the bug, then choose the fix.

topics.title: Functions
topics.lead: A function is a mini-program inside your program. Give a block of code a name, then run it as often as you like by calling that name.

acts.title: Follow the calls
acts.brief: In these programs, functions call other functions. Count carefully: how many times will the heart appear?

acts.title: Parameter playground
acts.brief: One function, different values. Add calls to flash_icon and watch what icon and delay hold each time the function runs.

acts.title: What comes back?
acts.brief: return sends a value back to the line that called the function. Work out what each call returns. Get 15 right to finish. Some calls put one function inside another.

acts.title: Assemble the function
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: Read the pseudocode
acts.brief: Read the plan, then pick the Python that follows it. FUNCTION … WITH is def with parameters, RETURN is return, and CALL runs the function.

acts.title: Quick quiz: functions
acts.brief: Defining, calling, parameters and return. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program has one bug in how a function is defined, called or returns a value. Find the line, then choose the fix.

topics.title: Event Loop
topics.lead: while True: repeats its code forever. Each time round, the program can check for events such as button presses and respond to them.

acts.title: Inside or outside?
acts.brief: Each program has the right lines but the wrong indentation. Use the → and ← buttons to move lines inside or outside the loop, then run it.

acts.title: Follow the flowchart
acts.brief: Press ▶ Start and watch the highlighted shape move along the arrows. When it stops at a diamond, read the question under Now and click Yes or No (or press Y or N).

acts.title: Build the flowchart
acts.brief: Each lettered shape is blank. Choose what goes in it so the flowchart matches the code. Indented lines go inside the loop; lines before while True go above it.

acts.title: Which code matches?
acts.brief: Indentation changes the shape of the flowchart.

acts.title: Read the pseudocode
acts.brief: Read the plan, then pick the Python that follows it line for line. Pay attention to what comes before, inside and after the loop.

acts.title: Translate it
acts.brief: Choose the Python for each line of the plan. Your program builds up on the right as you go.

acts.title: Write the pseudocode
acts.brief: Build the pseudocode for a program by picking its steps in the right order.

acts.title: Dry run the plan
acts.brief: Predict what the plan does, then watch a dry run. The trace table records every line: the variables, each check, and the output.

acts.title: Find the error in the plan
acts.brief: Each plan has one mistake that stops it meeting its goal. Click the line with the error, then choose the fix.

acts.title: Complete the plan
acts.brief: Choose the right word, operator or value for each blank so the plan meets its goal. Then compare it with the Python.

acts.title: When does it break?
acts.brief: The loop counts up and stops with break. Predict the last number printed, then run it. Watch the difference between < and <=.

acts.title: Buttons in the loop
acts.brief: This program is running now. The loop checks the buttons over and over. Press A and B on the board (or the A and B keys).

acts.title: Quick quiz: loops
acts.brief: while True, indentation, break and buttons. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: What will it do?
acts.brief: Read each loop and predict what it prints or shows. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each loop has one bug. Look for missing colons, indentation and missing break lines.

title: Selection Lab
blurb: if, elif and else, and selection inside the event loop.
icon: data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'><rect width='64' height='64' rx='14' fill='%231b5fa8'/><text x='32' y='43' font-family='Menlo,Consolas,monospace' font-size='30' font-weight='700' fill='white' text-anchor='middle'>if</text></svg>
outcomes: Write conditions with comparison operators that are True or False
Choose between paths with if, elif and else
Follow and plan decisions with flowcharts and pseudocode
Check buttons and sensors inside the event loop and react to them

topics.title: Selection
topics.lead: Selection lets a program choose a path. A condition is either True or False, and that decides which block of code runs.

acts.title: Which path runs?
acts.brief: Read the program and pick what you think the micro:bit will do. Then watch it run: each condition is marked True or False as Python checks it.

acts.title: Follow the flowchart
acts.brief: Start at the top and follow the arrows. At each diamond, answer Yes or No for the situation shown. Outputs appear on the micro:bit as you pass them.

acts.title: Build the flowchart
acts.brief: Each lettered shape is blank. Choose what goes in it so the flowchart does exactly what the code does.

acts.title: Which code matches?
acts.brief: Read the flowchart, follow every Yes and No arrow, then pick the code with exactly the same structure: the same decisions, in the same order, with the same Yes and No paths.

acts.title: Read the pseudocode
acts.brief: Pseudocode is a plan in plain English. Read it, then pick the Python that follows it line for line. Watch for the order of the checks, int(), and = versus ==.

acts.title: Translate it
acts.brief: Choose the Python for each line of pseudocode. Your program builds up on the right as you go. Not every pseudocode line needs its own Python line.

acts.title: Write the pseudocode
acts.brief: Build the pseudocode for a program by picking its steps in the right order.

acts.title: Dry run the plan
acts.brief: Predict what the plan does, then watch a dry run. The trace table records every line: the variables, each check, and the output.

acts.title: Find the error in the plan
acts.brief: Each plan has one mistake that stops it meeting its goal. Click the line with the error, then choose the fix.

acts.title: Complete the plan
acts.brief: Choose the right word, operator or value for each blank so the plan meets its goal. Then compare it with the Python.

acts.title: Find the boundary
acts.brief: Drag the slider to change the variable. The conditions update as you drag, and the green bar shows which block would run.

acts.title: Ask the user
acts.brief: input() waits for the user to type something. Run the program, type an answer in the serial pane, and press Enter. Try to reach every target.

acts.title: Assemble the decision
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: True or False?
acts.brief: Every if depends on a condition that is either True or False. Work out what each comparison prints. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Quick quiz: selection
acts.brief: Conditions, if, elif, else and input. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program has one bug. Read what it should do and what actually happens, click the line with the bug, then choose the fix.

topics.title: Selection in the Event Loop
topics.lead: Put an if inside while True: and the micro:bit keeps checking its buttons and sensors, reacting the moment something happens.

acts.title: Belongs to the if, or the loop?
acts.brief: A small change in indentation gives completely different behaviour.

acts.title: Follow the flowchart
acts.brief: Event loops have a loop-back arrow, so the path never reaches End. Each time you come back to a diamond, the situation may have changed: read the question carefully.

acts.title: Build the flowchart
acts.brief: Fill in the blank shapes so the flowchart matches the event loop. Watch where each line sits: inside the if (on the Yes arrow) or at loop level (on the main path).

acts.title: Which code matches?
acts.brief: Indentation changes the shape of the flowchart.

acts.title: Read the pseudocode
acts.brief: Read the plan for each event loop, then pick the Python that follows it line for line. Lines between REPEAT FOREVER and END REPEAT are inside the loop.

acts.title: Translate it
acts.brief: Choose the Python for each line of the plan. Indentation is added for you on the right, based on where each line sits in the plan.

acts.title: Write the pseudocode
acts.brief: Build the pseudocode for a program by picking its steps in the right order.

acts.title: Dry run the plan
acts.brief: Predict what the plan does, then watch a dry run. The trace table records every line: the variables, each check, and the output.

acts.title: Find the error in the plan
acts.brief: Each plan has one mistake that stops it meeting its goal. Click the line with the error, then choose the fix.

acts.title: Complete the plan
acts.brief: Choose the right word, operator or value for each blank so the plan meets its goal. Then compare it with the Python.

acts.title: Sensor lab
acts.brief: These are the programs from the slides. Pick one, press Run, then use the buttons, sliders and clap to set it off. Change a threshold to see how it changes the behaviour.

acts.title: Quick quiz: what will it do?
acts.brief: Buttons, sensors, sound and indentation. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Assemble the event loop
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: When does it react?
acts.brief: Each condition reads a button or a sensor. Work out exactly which values make it react. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each event loop has one bug. Look closely at indentation, comparison signs and sensor ranges.

title: Loops Lab
blurb: while loops and for loops with range().
icon: data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'><rect width='64' height='64' rx='14' fill='%231b5fa8'/><text x='32' y='43' font-family='Menlo,Consolas,monospace' font-size='30' font-weight='700' fill='white' text-anchor='middle'>↻</text></svg>
outcomes: Write a while loop with a start value, a condition and an update
Spot and fix loops that never stop
Use for loops with range() to repeat a set number of times
Convert a while loop into a for loop and pick the right loop for the job

topics.title: While loops
topics.lead: A while loop is like an if statement that repeats. It keeps running its body while the condition is True, and stops as soon as the condition is False.

acts.title: How many times?
acts.brief: Work out how many times the loop body runs, type your answer, then run it and watch the loop counter. Each check of the while line is marked True or False.

acts.title: Track, check, update
acts.brief: Every while loop that stops has three key parts. Click the line for each part, in order.

acts.title: Will it ever stop?
acts.brief: Decide what each loop will do: stop, run forever, or never run at all. Then watch it run. The simulator gives up after 25 times round.

acts.title: Predict the output
acts.brief: Read the while loop and pick what it prints. Then run it and watch the variables change each time round.

acts.title: Follow the flowchart
acts.brief: In a flowchart, the while line is a diamond. Yes runs the loop body, No leaves the loop, and the arrow on the left goes back to check again.

acts.title: Dry run the plan
acts.brief: Predict what the plan does, then watch a dry run fill in the trace table. A trace table is the best way to check a loop by hand.

acts.title: Find the error in the plan
acts.brief: Each plan has one mistake that stops it meeting its goal. Click the line with the error, then choose the fix.

acts.title: Quick quiz: while loops
acts.brief: Counting loops, conditions and infinite loops. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each while loop has one bug: a missing colon, the wrong comparison, an update in the wrong place… Click the line, then choose the fix.

topics.title: For loops
topics.lead: A for loop is cleaner when you know how many times to repeat. It creates the counter, updates it, and stops at the right time, all in one line.

acts.title: Range explorer
acts.brief: Change the start, stop and step to see exactly which numbers range() gives. Hit every target. The stop number is never included.

acts.title: Predict the output
acts.brief: Read the for loop and pick what it will do. Then run it and watch the loop variable change each time round.

acts.title: How many times?
acts.brief: Work out how many numbers the range() gives, which is how many times the loop body runs. Type your answer, then run it and watch the loop counter.

acts.title: Convert it: while → for
acts.brief: Each while loop on the left can be written as a shorter for loop. Pick the one that goes through exactly the same numbers.

acts.title: Which loop?
acts.brief: For each job, decide which loop fits best. Do you know how many times it repeats, or does it depend on something that happens?

acts.title: Follow the flowchart
acts.brief: A for loop as a flowchart: the diamond asks whether range() has any numbers left. Each Yes hands out the next number.

acts.title: Translate it
acts.brief: Choose the Python for each line of the plan. In pseudocode, FROM 1 TO 5 includes 5. In Python, range() always stops one before.

acts.title: Complete the plan
acts.brief: Choose the right number, keyword or step for each blank so the plan meets its goal. Then compare it with the Python.

acts.title: Quick quiz: for loops
acts.brief: range(), loop variables and choosing the right loop. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each for loop has one bug, often in the range() numbers. Click the line, then choose the fix.

title: Data Types & Strings Lab
blurb: int, float, str and bool, then working with strings.
icon: data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'><rect width='64' height='64' rx='14' fill='%231b5fa8'/><text x='32' y='43' font-family='Menlo,Consolas,monospace' font-size='30' font-weight='700' fill='white' text-anchor='middle'>Aa</text></svg>
outcomes: Tell int, float, str and bool values apart and predict the result of each operator
Convert between types with int(), float() and str(), and know that input() always gives a string
Measure a string, change its case and replace part of it with built-in functions and methods
Find and fix type errors in micro:bit programs

topics.title: Letters and numbers
topics.lead: Use numbers to calculate and strings for text. Python decides the type from the value you write, and quotes make all the difference.

acts.title: What type is it?
acts.brief: Integers are whole numbers, floats have a decimal point, and strings are text in quotes. Sort each value: watch out for numbers in quotes.

acts.title: Add or join?
acts.brief: + adds numbers but joins strings, and * repeats strings. Predict what each program prints, then run it. The Variables panel shows each value's type.

acts.title: What type is the result?
acts.brief: Each line works something out. Decide what type the answer is: int, float or str. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Type casting
acts.brief: Each program needs one expression where the ??? is. Pick the one that meets the goal. Wrong choices run too, so you can see exactly what goes wrong.

acts.title: Input is always a string
acts.brief: input() always gives back text, even when you type a number. Run each program, type answers in the serial pane, and hit every target.

acts.title: Assemble the program
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: Quick quiz: data types
acts.brief: Numbers, strings and converting between them. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program mixes up its types somewhere. Click the line with the bug, then choose the fix.

topics.title: Strings
topics.lead: A string is a sequence of characters. Python has built-in functions and methods to measure it, change its case and replace part of it.

acts.title: String function explorer
acts.brief: Type any text, choose a function and see the result straight away, with the Python that does it. Hit every target.

acts.title: Count the characters
acts.brief: How many characters does len() count? Type your answer and check. Every character is then shown in its own box, and spaces are highlighted.

acts.title: Predict the output
acts.brief: What does each string function give back? Predict, then run it and check the Variables panel.

acts.title: Pick the expression
acts.brief: Each program needs one expression where the ??? is. Pick the one that prints exactly the goal. Wrong choices run too, so you can see what they really do.

acts.title: Strings and input
acts.brief: Programs that use string functions on what the user types, starting with two from the slides.

acts.title: Assemble the program
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: Quick quiz: strings
acts.brief: len(), upper(), lower() and replace(). Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program uses a string function wrongly. Click the line with the bug, then choose the fix.

title: Lists Lab
blurb: Building and changing lists, and looping over them.
icon: data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'><rect width='64' height='64' rx='14' fill='%231b5fa8'/><text x='32' y='43' font-family='Menlo,Consolas,monospace' font-size='26' font-weight='700' fill='white' text-anchor='middle'>[ ]</text></svg>
outcomes: Create lists and read items by their index
Add, change and remove items
Loop through a list to print, total or filter its items
Avoid index errors at the ends of a list

topics.title: Lists
topics.lead: A list stores many values in a single variable, like a row of numbered boxes. Perfect for collections such as sensor readings or names.

acts.title: Boxes and indexes
acts.brief: Picture a list as a row of boxes, numbered from 0. Click the box each question asks for.

acts.title: What's at that index?
acts.brief: Read each list and work out what the code gives back. Watch out for an index that doesn't exist.

acts.title: List playground
acts.brief: Lists can grow and shrink. Use the buttons to change the list and watch the boxes and the Python. Hit every target, including the errors.

acts.title: Predict the list
acts.brief: Each program changes a list. Predict what's printed, then run it and watch the list in the Variables panel.

acts.title: Assemble the program
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: Translate it
acts.brief: Choose the Python for each line of the plan. ADD … TO THE END OF is append(), and the first item is always index 0.

acts.title: Quick quiz: lists
acts.brief: Indexes, list functions and len(). Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program uses a list wrongly. Click the line with the bug, then choose the fix.

topics.title: Lists and loops
topics.lead: Loops are the natural way to work through every item in a list: to print them, add them up, or build a new list from the ones you want.

acts.title: Loop through a list
acts.brief: Lists and loops go hand in hand. Predict what each loop prints, then watch the loop variable change in the Variables panel.

acts.title: Temperature logger
acts.brief: The slides' program: it appends a reading every second while the temperature is below 25, then prints them all with a for loop.

acts.title: Dry run the plan
acts.brief: Predict what each plan displays, then watch the trace table record every step through the list.

acts.title: Which loop works?
acts.brief: Each goal has three attempts. Pick the loop that does exactly what the goal asks. The others are off by one, crash, or print too much.

acts.title: Complete the plan
acts.brief: Choose the right word, number or symbol for each blank so the plan meets its goal. Then compare it with the Python.

acts.title: Quick quiz: lists and loops
acts.brief: Looping through lists with for and range(len()). Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each loop over a list has one bug, often an index that's off by one. Click the line, then choose the fix.

title: File Lab
blurb: Reading, writing and appending to files.
icon: data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 64 64'><rect width='64' height='64' rx='14' fill='%231b5fa8'/><text x='32' y='43' font-family='Menlo,Consolas,monospace' font-size='30' font-weight='700' fill='white' text-anchor='middle'>f</text></svg>
outcomes: Write text to a file and read it back with open() and with
Pick the right file mode and know when 'w' wipes a file
Add to an existing file by reading it first and writing it back
List the files saved on the micro:bit with listdir()

topics.title: Reading and writing files
topics.lead: The micro:bit can save text in files on the device, and read it back later. Open a file in the right mode, and with closes it for you, even if an error occurs.

acts.title: Which mode?
acts.brief: For each job, choose the mode you would open the file with. Two of the four modes aren't used in the online micro:bit editor, but you should still know them.

acts.title: Predict the file
acts.brief: Predict what each program prints, then run it. The storage panel shows what's inside every file, and ↵ marks each \n.

acts.title: Choose the mode
acts.brief: Pick "r" or "w" for every open() so the program meets its goal, then run it and watch the storage panel.

acts.title: Assemble the program
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: Translate it
acts.brief: Choose the Python for each line of the plan. FOR WRITING is "w", FOR READING is "r", and ⏎ is \n.

acts.title: Quick quiz: files
acts.brief: The slides' quiz plus a few more. Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program has one file mistake: a wrong mode, a wrong name or a missing \n. Click the line with the bug, then choose the fix.

topics.title: Appending and listing files
topics.lead: Opening a file with 'w' wipes it. To add to a file in the online editor, read it first, write the old content back, then write the new text. listdir() shows which files exist.

acts.title: Simulate appending
acts.brief: The slides' append program and some broken versions of it. Predict what's printed, then watch the file change.

acts.title: What does listdir() show?
acts.brief: Predict the list of files. Remember main.py, your program, is always there.

acts.title: Assemble the append
acts.brief: Build the code by picking the scrambled lines in the right order.

acts.title: Dry run the plan
acts.brief: Predict what each plan prints, then watch the trace table follow what is inside the file after every step.

acts.title: Which program works?
acts.brief: Read the goal and what's already saved. Then pick the program that meets the goal exactly.

acts.title: Quick quiz: appending and listing
acts.brief: Simulating append and listdir(). Answer all of them correctly to finish.

acts.title: Spot the bug
acts.brief: Each program tries to append or list files but has one bug. Click the line, then choose the fix.
